==English==

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:hot|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|hot}}, {{m|enm|hoot}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hāt|t=hot}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*hait}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*haitaz|t=hot}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*keHy-|t=to heat; to become hot}}. 
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|yol|hoat}}, {{m|yol|hoate}}, {{m|yol|hote|t=hot}}, {{cog|fy|hjit}}, {{m|fy|hyt|t=hot}}, {{cog|bar|hoaß|t=hot}}, {{cog|gmw-cfr|heeß|t=hot}}, {{cog|nl|heet|t=hot}}, {{cog|de|heiss}}, {{m|de|heiß}}, {{m|de|heyß|t=hot}}, {{cog|wym|haas}}, {{m|wym|haes}}, {{m|wym|hȧś}}, {{m|wym|hǡs|t=hot}}, {{cog|yi|הייס|t=hot}}, {{cog|da|hed|t=hot}}, {{cog|fo,is|heitur|t=hot}}, {{cog|nb,sv|het|t=hot}}; also {{cog|lt|kaitra|t=heat}}. Related to [[heat]].
{{col-bottom}}

Superseded non-native {{ncog|enm|chaud}}, from {{ncog|fro|chaut|t=hot}}; and early Modern {{ncog|en|calent}}, from {{ncog|la|calēns|t=hot}}.

===Adjective===
{{en-adj|er}}

# {{n-g|Relating to [[heat]] and conditions which produce it.}}
## {{lb|en|of an object}} Having or giving off a [[high]] [[temperature]].
##: {{syn|en|heated|Thesaurus:hot}}
##: {{ant|en|cold|chilled|Thesaurus:cold}}
##: {{ux|en|He forgot that the frying pan was '''hot''' and burned his hand.}}
##: {{ux|en|It is too '''hot''' to be outside.}}
##: {{ux|en|It is '''hotter''' in summer than in winter.}}
##: {{ux|en|It is roasting '''hot''' in here. Crack a window, please.}}
##* {{RQ:Christie Autobiography|II|4|passage=There was also hairdressing: hairdressing, too, really was hairdressing in those times — no running a comb through it and that was that. It was curled, frizzed, waved, put in curlers overnight, waved with '''hot''' tongs;{{nb...}}.}}
##* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Hiufu Wong|title=11 extreme weather records|url=https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/extreme-weather-records/index.html|date=2017-06-15|passage=“Everybody is interested in extremes – the '''hottest''', the wettest, the windiest – so creating a database of professionally verified records is useful in that fact alone,” says Randall Cerveny from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250930134223/https://www.cnn.com/travel/article/extreme-weather-records/index.html|archivedate=30 September 2025}}
##* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Jack Healy; Sophie Kasakove|title=A Drought So Dire That a Utah Town Pulled the Plug on Growth|date=2021-07-20|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/07/20/us/utah-water-drought-climate-change.html|passage=It is one of the first towns in the United States to purposely stall growth for want of water in a new era of megadroughts. But it could be a harbinger of things to come in a '''hotter''', drier West.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260203100857/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/07/20/us/utah-water-drought-climate-change.html|archivedate=3 February 2026}}
## {{lb|en|of a [[person]] or [[animal]]}} Feeling the sensation of [[heat]], especially to the point of discomfort.
##: {{ux|en|I was so '''hot''' from being in the sun too long.}}
##: {{ux|en|Aren't you '''hot''' with that thick coat on?}}
## [[feverish|Feverish]]; feeling a high [[fever]].
# [[active|Active]], in use or ready for use (like a bullet or a firing range), turned on (like a microphone or camera).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=Larry Munson; Tony Barnhart|title=From Herschel to a Hobnail Boot: The Life and Times of Larry Munson|publisher=Triumph Books|isbn=9781623686826|page=52
|passage=So I just blurted out, "This is really a fucking way to make a living, huh?" {{...}} The microphone was '''hot''', and I knew I was in trouble. The radio management came to my house and suspended me immediately.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=Don Carpenter|title=The Hollywood Trilogy: A Couple of Comedians, The True Story of Jody McKeegan, and Turnaround|publisher=Catapult|isbn=9781619024090
|passage=I leaned forward, still ogling, thinking the camera was off me until the end of the song, but then on went the little red light that meant my camera was '''hot''' ...}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2017|author=Charles Henderson|title=Terminal Impact|publisher=Penguin|isbn=9781101988145|page=8
|passage="Your range is '''hot''', corporal. Wind unchanged. You've got your dope. Fire at will," Hacksaw said, snapping the camera as fast as the motor drive could run ...}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2017|author=Scott Kelly|title=Endurance: My Year in Space, A Lifetime of Discovery|publisher=Vintage|isbn=9781524731601
|passage=I join the space-to-ground channel to warn Terry that his mic is '''hot''' and that everyone with an internet connection or tuned to NASA TV can hear every word ...}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2020|author=A.J. Stone|title=Project Titan|publisher=Page Publishing Inc|isbn=9781662413711
|passage="The range is hot, chief. Fire at will." Alex says with a smile as he steps back and puts his shooting ear muffs on. "I'm going to shoot, major."}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2020|author=Ferrett Steinmetz|title=Automatic Reload: A Novel|publisher=Tor Books|isbn=9781250168207
|passage=I run an inventory, verify all bullets are '''hot''' in the chamber. They are. But the showroom prosthetics have all exited attraction mode.}}
## {{lb|en|US|uncomparable}} [[electrically|Electrically]] [[charged]].
##: {{syn|en|live}}
##: {{ant|en|neutral|dead}}
##: {{ux|en|a '''hot''' wire}}
## {{lb|en|informal}} [[radioactive|Radioactive]]. {{defdate|from the 20th c.}}
## {{lb|en|figurative|of a factory or production line}} In active use at or near capacity.
##: {{ux|en|We need to keep the old drone production line going while it's still '''hot''', or it'll be difficult to restart it.}}
# {{lb|en|figurative}} {{n-g|Relating to excited emotions.}}
## {{lb|en|of a [[temper]]}} Easily provoked to [[anger]].
##: {{ux|en|Be careful, he has a '''hot''' temper and may take it out on you.}}
## {{senseid|en|physically or sexually attractive}} {{lb|en|colloquial|of a person}} [[physically|Physically]] or [[sexually]] [[attractive]].
##: {{alti|en|hawt|hott}}
##: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:attractive|Thesaurus:beautiful}}
##: {{ux|en| He saw many '''hot''' girls at the concert.}}
##: {{ux|en|That stripper is '''hot'''!}}
## {{lb|en|colloquial}} [[sexual|Sexual]] or [[sexy]]; involving [[sexual intercourse]] or sexual [[excitement]].
##: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:sexy}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|title=Moving Toward The Light|author=Rick R. Reed|page=50|passage=There was only one problem. Paul was HIV positive. And just a few weeks after his '''hot''' encounter with Max, a letter arrived for him, containing some legalese about HIV infection being a criminal act, with a few chilling words|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=ZFgQKJ5LovwC&pg=PA50|ISBN=1609824288}}
## {{lb|en|slang}} [[sexual|Sexual]]ly aroused; [[randy]].
##: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:sexually aroused}}
##: {{ux|en|Enough foreplay! You’ve gotten me so '''hot''' already!}}
## {{lb|en|slang}} Extremely attracted to. {{+obj|en|:for}}
##: {{ux|en|'''hot''' for her English teacher}}
# {{n-g|Relating to popularity, quality, or the state of being interesting.}}
## {{lb|en|informal}} Very good, remarkable, exciting. {{defdate|from the 19th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|He's a '''hot''' young player; we should give him a trial.}}
## [[popular|Popular]]; [[in demand]].
##: {{ux|en|This new pickup is so '''hot''' we can't keep it in stock!}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|author=Andy Bradley; Roger Wood|title=House of Hits|page=206
|passage=And in 1975 one of the '''hottest''' Austin ensembles was the posthippie western swing revivalist group known as Asleep at the Wheel.}}
## Of great [[current]] [[interest]]; provoking current [[debate]] or [[controversy]].
##: {{co|en|a '''hot''' topic}}
## [[performing|Performing]] strongly; having [[repeated]] [[successes]] (i.e. having a winning or [[hot streak]]).
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Peter Krause; Andy King|title=Play-By-Play Golf|publisher=First Avenue Editions|page=55
|passage=The ball lands on the fairway, just a couple of yards in front of the green. "Nice shot Sarah! You're '''hot''' today!" Jenny says.}}
## [[fresh|Fresh]]; just [[released]].
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1960|title=Super Markets of the Sixties: Findings, recommendations.- v.2. The plans and sketches|author=Super Market Institute|page=30
|passage=A kid can stand in the street and sell newspapers, if the headlines are '''hot'''.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2000|author=David Cressy|title=Travesties and transgressions in Tudor and Stuart England: tales of discord and dissension|page=34|publisher=Oxford University Press
|passage=Some of these publications show signs of hasty production, indicating that they were written while the news was '''hot'''.}}
## {{lb|en|programming|of code}} {{U|frequently}} [[execute]]d.
##: {{ux|en|Optimise '''hot''' code paths first.}}
# {{n-g|Relating to danger or risk.}}
## [[uncomfortable|Uncomfortable]], difficult to deal with; [[awkward]], [[dangerous]], [[unpleasant]].
##* {{quote-book|en|title=The shadow in the sands|page=68|author=Sam Llewellyn|year=1999|passage=The police are looking for an anarchist who answers my description, seen leaving the house the day before the fire; there was an explosion{{...}}So what with one thing and another, His Grace thinks the country a little '''hot''' for me now}}
## {{lb|en|slang}} Characterized by [[police]] [[presence]] or [[activity]].
##: {{ux|en|I wouldn't speed through here if I was you. This area is '''hot''' this time of night.}}
## {{senseid|en|stolen}} {{lb|en|slang}} [[steal|Stolen]]. {{defdate|from the 20th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|'''hot''' merchandise}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|author=Robert Eversz|title=Burning Garbo: A Nina Zero Novel|publisher=Simon and Schuster|isbn=9780743253567|page=17
|passage=The camera was '''hot'''. Buying a '''hot''' camera was a parole violation.}}
## {{lb|en|not comparable|slang|of a [[draft]] or [[check]]}} Not [[cover]]ed by [[funds]] on [[account]].
##: {{syn|en|rubber|bad}}
##: {{ux|en|I wouldn't trust him. He gave me a '''hot''' check last week.}}
## {{lb|en|slang|of bodily fluids}} Containing drugs.
##: {{ux|en|The soldier was discharged from the military after he pissed '''hot''' for cocaine.}}
# Very [[close]] to [[find]]ing or [[guess]]ing something to be found or guessed.
#: {{ux|en|Am I warm yet?'' — ''You're '''hot'''!}}
#: {{ux|en|He was '''hot''' on her tail.}}
# {{lb|en|of food}} [[spicy|Spicy]], [[pungent]], [[piquant]], as some [[chili]]s and other spices are.
#: {{ant|en|bland|mild}}
#: {{ux|en|This kind of chili pepper is way too '''hot''' for my taste.}}
# {{lb|en|acoustics}} [[loud|Loud]], producing a strong electric signal for the amplifier or other [[sound#Noun|sound]] equipment.
# {{lb|en|slang}} {{n-g|Used to emphasize the short duration or small quantity of something}}
#: {{ux|en|He was finished in a '''hot''' minute.}}
#: {{ux|en|I dated him for a '''hot''' second.}}
# {{lb|en|slang|of a [[vehicle]] or [[aircraft]]}} Extremely fast or with great [[speed]].
#: {{ux|en|That plane's coming in '''hot'''!}}
#: {{ux|en|a '''hot''' pass}}
